cells.tense: You are here with the work, and the careful thinking is holding steady.
cells.ask: Finish one decision you've been circling and act on it today — a call, a yes, a no — because the pieces have already said what they have to say.
cells.core: You're in the middle of a private read on something that's going well. Nothing's being rushed and nothing's being skipped — you keep turning it over until the parts that matter separate from the noise, and then you move. That habit runs on release, and release is what you're doing: the thing you put down stops taking up room, and you can see what's left standing. It looks like a quiet stretch because most of this happens where nobody sees it. The work only lands when the last step happens — the putting down. One more decision finished and off your hands is what the strength is for. It doesn't stay without that. The attention stays clean by being used on something real, and there's a decision in front of you right now that's finished except for the part where you act on it.
cells.sheetLine: You sort it out, then you set it down. That's the strength.
cells.verb: sorting what matters from what doesn't until the distinction is sharp enough to act on
cells.place: at the point where you decide what to set down and what to keep carrying

cells.tense: You are already living past a decision that hasn't been made yet.
cells.ask: Say out loud where one decision actually stands right now, before the next round of checking. Just where it is, not where it's going.
cells.core: You're checking and re-checking something that's already been checked, and the checking has a life of its own now. Every angle gets worked one more time because you're bracing for how it'll be judged, for the part you might have missed — so the work that was private has started needing an audience that isn't here yet. This kind of careful reading is a good thing until it starts running on its own, and somewhere in there it stopped being about the question and started being about not getting caught out. Everything gets tested against a verdict nobody has given. The sharpness is still there. What's gone is the last step it needs, the one where you decide it's done and put the question down. Until that happens the checking has no finish line.
cells.sheetLine: You're not sorting anymore. You're bracing.

cells.tense: You made a decision once and you're still standing at the point where it was made.
cells.ask: Open the thing you decided once and check one fact you'd know if you trusted yourself. Just look, say what's there.
cells.core: Something got decided, and you haven't exactly gone back on it, but you haven't moved past the moment either. The reasoning was good enough and then it stopped — like the putting down didn't finish, so you're standing at the edge with your hands still full. You're still turning that over when it comes up, checking whether the ground holds before you step. The old reading still works, technically. It just isn't doing anything anymore, and it doesn't feel finished because it isn't. The step from sorted to released hasn't happened, and more looking doesn't get you there. What gets you there is different air on it — a fresh set of eyes, someone who can tell you what they see without needing your version first.
cells.sheetLine: You decided, but you haven't put it down yet.

cells.tense: You are already letting things go, and you'd tell it as just trimming what's practical.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've stopped doing and say plainly that you chose to stop. One sentence, to yourself, naming it as a choice.
cells.core: You've been making the call on what stays and what goes for longer than you'd say out loud. Some old version of this got dropped — the part where you did it differently — and you've moved on without marking the moment: you'd call the change just what the situation required. The calls keep happening anyway. They shape what you pick up, what you let pass, what you don't bother showing anyone because there's no need. The call was made. The saying-so didn't happen. That's the piece still hanging — you keep choosing from a decision you haven't admitted making, and until you call it yours the choice keeps getting filed under circumstances. Call one of those calls yours, out loud or on paper, and the rest of it lines up.
cells.sheetLine: You let it go already. You still call it trimming.

attempts.check: The record doesn't say the person has a habit of holding on, so the Balanced cell locates release only in moments they could recognise, not in a pattern. A reader could reasonably say the sorting they do is just worrying, which is why the Too Much cell keeps the mechanism to checking a call before it's made. The asks stay doable if the read is wrong — one decision finished, one thing put down — because each asks for an act, not a verdict. The sentence that serves me is any line about setting something down; it sounds wise and tells them nothing, so it's gone.
